raw: {"vote":"better","margin":"slight","reason":"AFTER更清楚地限定了参考素材职责、未绑定素材和非首帧用法，减少了臆造与错误提交风险，但在案例一中牺牲了部分具体动作和场景细节。","case_notes":["案例一：AFTER对缺失狼素材和未核验剧本内容处理更稳健，但“按剧本规定”使样本的可执行性和视觉具体性弱于BEFORE。","案例二：AFTER的批次范围、分段时序、素材职责和非首帧约束表达更清晰，整体略优于内容相近的BEFORE。"]}

{"vote":"better","margin":"slight","reason":"AFTER improves resource-role correctness and fallback behavior by explicitly preventing invented visuals, bindings, or start-frame semantics, though it becomes somewhat less concrete and executable when screenplay details are unavailable.","case_notes":["Case 1: AFTER avoids BEFORE's unsupported forest, wolf appearance, and specific actions while clearly marking missing script and asset state, but loses some useful actionable specificity.","Case 2: AFTER more explicitly enforces each reference asset's role and non-start-frame use, with comparable sample gating and clearer anti-hallucination constraints."]}

{"vote":"better","margin":"slight","reason":"AFTER improves reference-role separation and material-binding correctness, while CASE 1 sacrifices some executable specificity for safer uncertainty handling.","case_notes":["CASE 1: BEFORE gives a more concrete and usable chase sample, but assumes Alia is callable and invents forest details; AFTER correctly treats unverified bindings and script details as unresolved, though its placeholders reduce action specificity.","CASE 2: AFTER more clearly separates each reference asset's responsibility and structures the sample into timed stages, while both appropriately stop at the required video-sample checkpoint despite the request for the full film."]}
